name: OSCURA
full_name: Observatory of Skipper CCDs Unveiling Recoiling Atoms
summary: OSCURA proposes to scale Skipper-CCD dark-matter searches to multiple kilograms, increasing exposure and tightening background-control requirements for light-dark-matter–electron scattering.
detection_principle: A large array of fully depleted silicon CCDs uses repeated nondestructive single-electron readout. Cryogenics, material screening and shielding suppress few-charge backgrounds.

sites.name: SNOLAB
sites.location: Underground laboratory in the Creighton mine, Sudbury, Ontario
sites.site_status: Deployment location proposed in the 2023 paper

status.label: Proposed
status.evidence: The 2023 device-requirements paper explicitly calls this a proposed experiment with planned SNOLAB deployment; evidence for a completed full detector has not been obtained.

results.summary: Sensor requirements and preliminary tests were reported; sensitivity curves are projections.

science_scope: This record covers experiments that directly measure possible interactions between dark matter and ordinary matter. Published exclusion limits, background events and projected sensitivities do not constitute a dark-matter discovery.

media.caption: Liquid-nitrogen pressure vessel, stacked supermodules and internal lead/copper shielding in an early OSCURA concept (2022 white paper, Figure 6). This is not a completed detector.
